seed_claims.claim: SEED 7.4: gauge a U(1) inside the internal symmetry and read off the folds' electric charges
seed_claims.evidence: Q = I3 + Y/2 with the WZ constraint Y_R = N_c B/3; every state of 8, 10, 10bar, 27 has an integer charge (Gell-Mann-Nishijima); SU(2): Q = I3 + B/2, the isoscalar half from the gauged WZ term. Needs N_c = 3 with standard quark charges (or anomaly-consistent charges). Predicts exotic charges (Theta+, Xi--, Q = +-2 in the 27).

seed_claims.claim: SEED 7.4 / 2: one cone, no vacuum dispersion; photon and fold field share it
seed_claims.evidence: pion omega^2 = k^2 + m^2, photon omega = |k| (two transverse modes), no mixing; Skyrme and gauged WZ terms have no quadratic part (both computed). Holds by construction for a Lorentz-invariant tree-level Lagrangian.

seed_claims.claim: Commitment 1: vacuum T_mu nu proportional to g_mu nu, p = -rho in every frame
seed_claims.evidence: T_mu nu = V0 g_mu nu (mostly-minus) at U = 1; V0 is a free constant.

seed_claims.claim: Commitment 4: charge is dressed (effective charge depends on how closely you look), not slowed
seed_claims.verdict: CONFIRMED (in the preregistered operational sense only)
seed_claims.evidence: Preregistered prediction holds: with massless pions the isovector <r^2> inside R grows as 0.411 fm x R (diverges); finite with m_pi = 138 MeV. Enclosed proton charge 0.34 at 0.5 fm, 0.76 at 1 fm, 0.96 at 5 fm; the neutron's enclosed charge peaks at +0.206 at R = 0.73 fm (positive core, negative cloud). The test cannot tell 'dressing' from any extended charge distribution; the mechanism is the fold's classical pion cloud, not QED vacuum polarization; 'not slowed' holds by construction.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 6B: for nucleons the model lands within roughly 30% (ANW 1983)
seed_claims.evidence: Against PDG 2026 at the calibrated ANW point: 6 of 7 finite predictions within 33% (strictly within 30%: 3 of 7; mu_p -33%, mu_n -31%, g_piNN -32% sit just outside 30%). The amendment is carried by g_A (-52%, a factor ~2) and by r_p and <r^2>_n, which are infinite with massless pions. At the fold's own f_pi = F_pi/2 = 64.5 MeV (itself 30% below 92.2 MeV) the gauged WZ term gives Gamma(pi0->gg) = 2.03 x PrimEx-II.

seed_claims.claim: PLAN E5 internal-consistency prediction (not a SEED sentence): the fold sector and the anomaly prefer different f_pi
seed_claims.evidence: Gamma(pi0->gg) at the fold's f: 15.86 eV (ANW, 2.03 x PrimEx-II), 20.40 eV (SU(3) refit, 2.61 x); PrimEx-II needs f = 91.97 MeV. Bears on SEED 6B (one (F, e) for all predictions).

seed_claims.claim: SEED 2: the WZ term that makes the fold a fermion also fixes pi0 -> gamma gamma
seed_claims.verdict: CONFIRMED (the anomaly normalisation); the N_c = 1 exclusion holds only with fixed quark charges
seed_claims.evidence: Gamma = 7.761 eV at N_c = 3, f = 92.21 MeV (-0.35 sigma vs PrimEx-II). N_c = 1 gives 0.862 eV, excluded at 59 sigma only if quark charges are held at (2/3, -1/3), which also makes N_c = 1 baryon charges fractional; with anomaly-consistent charges the width does not depend on N_c.

symbolic_checks.check: U0 unitary on |n|=1, s^2+c^2=1
1b. energy density is spherically symmetric pointwise
2. L_kin = (lambda/2) W^2 with lambda = (2pi/3) int x^2 s^2 [1+4(F'^2+s^2/x^2)] dx
3b. 3x3 embedding reproduces I1 = lambda (same generator normalisation lambda_a/2)
3c. lambda_8 commutes with the embedded hedgehog (zero inertia, WZ-constrained)
4a. isospin charge density of the rotating hedgehog averages to lambda(r) W_a (I^N = lambda W)
4b. static isovector current has the form V^k_b = eps_{kbl} n_l g(r)
4c. hedgehog identity V^0_a = (W x x)_j V^j_a (rotation in isospace = rotation in space)
4d. (2/3) r g(r) = lambda density  =>  int r g d^3x = (3/2) lambda  =>  mu^{I=1}_p = lambda/6
5a. B^0 = kappa eps^{0ijk}Tr(L_i L_j L_k) = -(1/2pi^2) s^2 F'/r^2 with kappa = -1/(24*pi**2)
5b. B^k = B^0 (W x x)_k : the baryon current is rigidly transported by the physical rotation
5c. kappa = -1/(24 pi^2) exactly (magnitude = standard 1/(24 pi^2); the sign follows from eps^{0123}=+1, L = U^+ dU, B = +1)
6a. angular average of (1/2) x x (B/2 with B^0=1)(W x x) = r^2 W/6  =>  mu^{I=0} = <r^2> J/(6 lambda)
6b. (1/2) <eps_ijk x_j eps_kbl n_l> = (r/3) delta_ib  =>  mu^{I=1}_i = D_3i (1/3) int r g d^3x
7a. static axial current has the form A^j_a = f1(r) delta_aj + f2(r) n_a n_j
7b. derived axial density matches the D-formula with the literature sign: 4 pi (f1+f2/3) = -(pi/3) D
7c. tail: f1 -> -(C/4)/r^3, f2 -> +(3C/4)/r^3 (pion field ~ d_j(n_a/r^2)); g_A(tail) = 2 pi C/(3 e^2)
8a. ANW I_k and J_k obey the standard su(2) algebra [X1,X2] = i X3
8b. operator identity I_k = -D_kl(A) J_l holds on S^3 (hedgehog: isospin = -rotated spin)
9a. linear part of T_beta = i (3 Tr(Q^2 tau_3)) d_beta pi0 / f = i d_beta pi0 / f; pi+- do not couple (Tr Q^2 tau_{1,2} = 0)
9b. antisymmetrised product of three su(2) elements is proportional to 1 (so Q = I3 + (N_c/6) B: B/2 at N_c=3)
9c. Gamma(pi0->gg) from the gauged WZ term = alpha^2 m^3 N_c^2/(576 pi^3 f^2)
9d. amplitude coefficient A = N_c e^2/(12 pi^2 f) (= e^2/(4 pi^2 f) at N_c = 3, B-H eq. 70)
9e. equivalent effective coupling: L = g pi0 F_mu nu F~^{mu nu} with g = K = N_c e^2/(48 pi^2 f) (B-H eq. 69 2nd line has 24 pi^2: factor-2 F~ normalisation)
9f. amplitude factor N_c Tr(Q^2 tau3): fixed charges -> N_c/3 ; anomaly-consistent charges -> 1 (N_c-independent)
10a. quadratic part of (F^2/16)Tr(DU DU^+) = (1/2) d_mu pi^a d^mu pi^a (no photon-pion mixing at this order)
10b. quadratic part of the mass term = -(1/2) m_pi^2 pi^a pi^a
10c. L_mu = U^+ D_mu U vanishes at zeroth order, so the Skyrme term [L,L]^2 starts at 4th order (no quadratic part)
10d. gauged WZ term expanded in all fields: no part of order 0, 1 or 2 (no quadratic part; computed)
9g. that cubic part = (N_c e^2/(24 pi^2 f)) eps^{mu nu al be} d_mu A_nu A_al d_be pi0 = (N_c e^2/(48 pi^2 f)) eps F_mu nu A_al d_be pi0 (only pi0 couples)
10e. Maxwell: off the cone (k^2!=0) M(k) has rank 3, null space = pure gauge k^mu; on the cone rank 1 (two transverse photons + gauge)
10f. pion: omega^2 = k^2 + m^2, group velocity k/omega < 1 -> 1 as k -> oo; photon omega = |k| (phase=group=1)
10g. k^2 is boost invariant, so both dispersion relations hold in every frame (one cone, no preferred frame)
11a. vacuum (U=1, dU=0): T_mu nu = 2 dL/dg^{mu nu} - g_mu nu L = V0 g_mu nu (mostly-minus; = -V0 g in mostly-plus)
11b. rho = T_00 = V0 and p = T_11 = -V0: p = -rho (taut vacuum)
11c. boosted vacuum T_mu nu is unchanged (Lambda^T g Lambda = g): same in every frame
